title: The assayer verifies with a shell, isolated from the work
situation: Decision 0051 kept one tool restriction ahead of evidence: the assayer, which never repairs, gets no tool that changes anything, so no shell. Observed since: assayers in cuts 5 and leakage precision could only trace the work statically; they could not run a check, read the history of a change or reproduce a finding, and their leads ran the checks for them. Judgment rests on the assayer's own evidence (impartial, trust-but-verify); denying it the means to gather evidence weakens the verdict more than it protects the work. Independent verification in practice gets full means to examine and run the work, with independence held by separation, not by denial.
decision: The assayer gets the harness's default tools, its shell included, and is dispatched isolated from the work, in its own copy, so nothing it runs or changes can reach the work or the branch it judges; never-repairs is held by that isolation and by its guardrail. The concept journal's appending verbs stay withheld from it, since the journal is shared. This supersedes the assayer exception in 0051; reach otherwise still starts open and narrows from observed use.
consequences: Realized in the typed-handoffs cut (0064) with the lead's journal reach (0059), since all three are bindings of the same extension and declarations. Until then, a lead may run an assayer's requested checks and give it the output.
